newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha rises on ACCESS crude gains.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha rises on ACCESS crude gains.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha prices were notionally firmer in late afternoon trade on Wednesday, pulled up by crude oil gains on the ACCESS after-hours trading system, which was prompted by bullish U.S. inventory data released overnight.
"Prices are nominally higher, but we don't have enough firm players to find out where the real market levels are today," one naphtha broker said.
Open-spec naphtha was assessed at about $212.50/213.50 per tonne for first-half October delivery, up by $2.00 to $2.50 from late Tuesday's levels.
The contango in near-term spreads was little changed, with second-half September/second-half October quoted at minus 75 cents/even.

Naphtha spreads remained in contango in part because sliding prices for olefins and polyolefins, both of which are derived from naphtha, have depressed buying interest from regional petrochemical end-users, traders said.
For instance, polypropylene prices fell by about $50 to $670-$680 per tonne C&F Hong Kong over the last two weeks, and high density polyethylene by $20 to $780 a tonne, they said.
